text: #919, built by hand because it is the product's own setup path, and each of three independent reviews changed its shape. invariant new OWNER/NAME founds an empty project in one command. It creates the GitHub repository, private unless -public, and its checkout; writes a starter that is complete for Go, with a module, a format check that fails on differences, a README, SPEC.md, AGENTS.md, the spec at docs/PRD.md when -spec names one, the gate pinned to the commit -invariant names, and checks with nothing left unresolved; commits and pushes it; and requires the gate on main where the account's plan allows and main isn't protected already, saying what it means where it doesn't. It founds empty projects only. A directory that holds anything it doesn't write, a checkout whose repository is somewhere else, an origin that fetches from or pushes to another address, and a GitHub repository that already holds commits are refused before anything is created, and an existing repository is invariant init's. It decides by reading the directory itself, adds only its own files, pushes only a main that is its own single commit, runs git and gh without the variables, such as GIT_DIR, that tie git to one repository, and prints no message that tells a person to commit a file or to replace main's protection. A second run changes nothing. It acts on the owner's account, so a coding agent runs it only when asked. Not decided here: a New project form on the dashboard, and starters for TypeScript and Python.
